newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car stocks underperform weak Paris bourse.
newsitem.headline: French car stocks underperform weak Paris bourse.

text.p: Shares in French carmakers Renault SA and PSA Peugeot Citroen fell even more sharply on Thursday than the Paris bourse CAC index despite a December sales report that most analysts found in line with expectations or better.
Shares in Renault were down 3.5 percent at 107.60 francs, and PSA Peugeot Citroen shares were off 4.5 percent at 558 francs at 1510 GMT. The CAC was down 2.4 percent.

"The sales figures weren't too bad, and certainly not for the Peugeot group," said one analyst, who said he was not aware of any fundamental reason for the stock's sharp fall and noted the volume was a thin 65,488 shares.

Some traders said Peugeot's stock may be under pressure after having spiked higher in year-end window-dressing. On Christmas Eve, the stock rose to 604 francs, while Renault hit a historic low of 103 francs on December 23.

New car sales in France rose 1.8 percent in December from dismal prior-year levels, when car sales were disrupted by public transport strikes, and they finished up 10.5 percent for the full year, the French carmakers' association CCFA said.
Foreign car sales rose 19.9 percent, compared with an increase of 7.4 percent for the Peugeot group and 0.6 percent at Renault, the weaker of the two French car firms.
French newspapers headlined the domestic industry's market share decline in 1996, and the Figaro reported that a price war would drive Renault, Saab, Ford Europe and Citroen in the red.

A spokesman for the Peugeot group said the company had not forecast a loss for the Citroen division for 1996 or made any earnings prediction. It does not break out Citroen and Peugeot division results.

Renault has said it expects to lose money in 1996, and its stock has long been in the doldrums. Brokers have recently turned bearish on the Peugeot group, with Societe Generale dropping it from its favoured list last week.
